title: Setting Boundaries with a Demanding Parent
paragraphs: As an only child, Ihsan had spent years accommodating his mother's frequent, often unreasonable requests for his time, believing that filial devotion required near-constant availability regardless of his own competing responsibilities.

After reaching a point of genuine burnout, Ihsan consulted a counselor who helped him recognize that sustainable devotion required boundaries, rather than the unsustainable self-sacrifice he had been practicing for years.

Implementing these boundaries proved emotionally difficult, as his mother initially reacted with hurt and accusations of neglect, interpreting his new limits as a rejection of the closeness they had always shared.

Over several months of consistent, respectful boundary-setting, his mother gradually adjusted her expectations, and their relationship, while different from before, became considerably more sustainable and genuinely less resentful on Ihsan's part.
